subsystems.name: Habitat tube
subsystems.role: the pressurised shell whose inner surface is the living area; spinning it about its long axis supplies artificial gravity.
parts: soil and water layer for shielding and growing

subsystems.name: Bearings and joints
subsystems.role: let neighbouring lengths of tube spin at different rates while still passing people and cargo between them.

subsystems.name: Orbit track
subsystems.role: holds the coiled tube in a stable path around the star so it neither falls in nor drifts away.

subsystems.name: Spin and momentum management
subsystems.role: spins segments up to operating speed and keeps the whole system balanced.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: collects starlight and dumps waste heat, which is hard in vacuum.

subsystems.name: Material supply and life support
subsystems.role: builds and sustains the habitat from non-terrestrial material.
parts: closed-loop air, water and food recycling

buildSteps.title: Choose the orbit and the radius
buildSteps.detail: A small tube radius keeps structural stress low. At 1 km radius, 1 g needs a rim speed near 99 m/s — about one rotation per minute — which ordinary steel could tolerate in hoop tension; the same habitat at 100 km radius would need far stronger material.

buildSteps.title: Mine material where it already is
buildSteps.detail: Bulk mass comes from asteroids or small moons rather than being lifted from a planet, because the required tonnage is astronomical.

buildSteps.title: Refine and form it in space
buildSteps.detail: Ore is processed with solar heat and power into metal sheet, structural members and shielding slag at a construction station.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate tube segments
buildSteps.detail: Short pressurised cylinders are welded or wound up individually, with windows, bearing races and attachment points built in.

buildSteps.title: Spin and balance each segment
buildSteps.detail: Segments are spun up separately and their internal mass arranged so each is dynamically balanced before anything is joined.

buildSteps.title: Couple segments with bearings
buildSteps.detail: Neighbouring segments meet at high-capacity bearings that allow relative rotation while carrying the loads between them.

buildSteps.title: Extend the tube into a coil
buildSteps.detail: The chain of segments is placed in orbit and lengthened turn by turn around the star; each turn is an independent orbit, so the structure is never a single rigid ring and the joins are not carrying the whole system's orbital loads.

buildSteps.title: Commission and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Atmosphere, ecosystems and shielding are brought online, and worn segments are swapped out individually — a closed loop where old material is recycled into new tube.

prerequisites.why: partial recycling has been demonstrated in orbit, but a habitat this size must approach full closure of air, water and food.

prerequisites.tech: In-space mining and manufacturing at scale
prerequisites.why: building from launched material alone is unaffordable; the structure must be made from asteroid or lunar mass.
kilometre-scale joints that spin continuously for decades under load do not exist.
cosmic rays and micrometeoroids require metres of mass shielding, which the tube itself can supply if designed for it.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap access to orbit and beyond
prerequisites.why: reusable launch has cut costs, but nothing yet approaches the cost per kilogram such a project needs.

pathway.milestone: orbiting stations and microgravity research; small rotating-habitat experiments
pathway.unlocks: experience of living and working in space for long periods.

pathway.milestone: free-flying rotating stations at a few metres to a few hundred metres radius
pathway.unlocks: verified artificial gravity, bearings and large pressure structures.

pathway.milestone: cylindrical habitats built mainly from off-Earth material, of the kind proposed in 1970s studies
pathway.unlocks: industrial-scale space manufacturing and closed ecosystems.

pathway.milestone: a single long tube in orbit — one link of the future topopolis
pathway.unlocks: proof that spinning segments can be coupled and extended.

pathway.milestone: extension into a coil of many turns around the star
pathway.unlocks: habitable area to rival or exceed a planet's surface without any single enormous structure — for example, a tube 1 km in radius and one astronomical unit long would enclose roughly 900 million square kilometres, about twice Earth's surface area.
